title: The Persian Qanat (Qasabeh qanat, Gonabad)
summary: The Persian Qanat is a UNESCO property of eleven qanats, underground channels that carry water by gravity from valley heads across arid Iran, inscribed in 2016. This record pins the Qasabeh qanat at Gonabad in Razavi Khorasan, which ICOMOS describes as over 13 km long with 222 wells and a 200 m deep mother well. Its age is uncertain: sources give 700-500 BCE or the 3rd-4th centuries BCE.

uncertainty.note: Kayhan Life says built between 700 and 500 BC; the ICOMOS evaluation says Qasabeh dates from 3-4 centuries BCE; Tehran Times says more than 2,000 years old. The range spans 700 to about 300 BCE. End is the present: the qanat is still active.

reviewer_note: The record covers the eleven-qanat property but the pin and model are ONE structure, the Qasabeh qanat, using the ICOMOS figures for its Qasabeh branch (over 13 km, 222 wells, 200 m mother well). Other pages give 33 km, 427 or 472 wells and 320 m for the combined Qasabeh and Doolab-e system, so they were kept out of the model. Shape wall with linear true is a stand-in: a qanat is underground, so "height" is recorded as depth of the mother well and should not be extruded upward. Dates conflict (700-500 BCE vs 3-4 centuries BCE). Pin is an OSM attraction node and could be the town-end rather than the mother well. Qasabeh qanat figures (not modelled: an underground channel): length 13000 m (src-icomos-qanat); height 200 m (src-icomos-qanat).
